div.p: A required child element of maintenanceEvent that provides the name of a person, institution, or system responsible for a specific event in the EAS instance's maintenance history, such as its creation, modification, or deletion. Also available in narrativeEvent to name a person, institution, or other type of agent of importance to the history of the CPF entity being described.

An element that provides the name of a person, institution, or other type of agent related to the archival materials being described or relevant to the EAS instance itself or any instantiation of it, e.g. a printed or online finding aid. Also available in narrativeEvent to name a person, institution, or other type of agent of importance to the history and processing of the materials being described.

A required child element of maintenanceEvent that provides the name of a person, institution, or system responsible for a specific event in the EAS instance's maintenance history, such as its creation, modification, or deletion.

Use agent to indicate the person, institution, or system responsible for a maintenance event. Examples include the name of the author or encoder, the database responsible for creating the EAS instance, and the style sheet used to update an instance to a new version of the EAS. Each maintenanceEvent element must have a child agent element. Use agent as an optional sub-element in narrativeEvent to name a person, institution, or other type of agent of importance to a specific event in the history of the CPF entity being described.

agent is a required and repeatable sub-element of agents and can be used to name persons, organizations, and families related to the archival materials being described as well as their specific relationship with and role towards the materials. The required sub-element label is used to encode the name of the agent, while the optional agentType and role allow for specifying the type of agent in question and for providing information about their role in relation to the materials being described (e.g., if a person is the "creator" of the materials or a "contributor" or if they are the "director" or the "cinematographer" of audiovisual material or the "defendant" or the "plaintiff" in court records). Use the sub-elements relationship, date, dateRange, or dateSet, and placeName along with the optional descriptiveNote to describe the relationship between the agent and the materials being described in more detail.

Use agent as a required sub-element of maintenanceEvent to name and describe the person, institution, or system responsible for a maintenance event. Examples include the name of the author or encoder, the database responsible for creating the EAS instance, and the style sheet used to update an instance to a new version of the EAS. Use agent as an optional and repeatable sub-element of findAidDesc to indicate any person, institution, or system relevant to the creation, publication, or disseminiation of any instantiations of the EAS instance such as the author, publisher, or sponsor of a printed or online finding aid. Use agent as an optional sub-element in narrativeEvent to name a person, institution, or other type of agent of importance to a specific event in the history or the processing of materials being described.

Use agent as a required sub-element of maintenanceEvent to name and describe the person, institution, or system responsible for a maintenance event. Examples include the name of the author or encoder, the database responsible for creating the EAS instance, and the style sheet used to update an instance to a new version of the EAS.
The prescribed order of all child elements (both required and optional) is:

list.item: One of date, dateRange, or dateSet

div.p: Use the agentType attribute to specify whether the agent is, for example, a "corporateBody", "mechanism", or "person". Use the optional agentTypeEncoding in control to specify the source or rules for values supplied in agentType.

Use the attributes valueURI, vocabularySource, and vocabularySourceURI with agent when referencing an entry of an external vocabulary, thesaurus, ontology applicable to the agent overall. In case of referencing different vocabularies or different entries within the same vocabulary for the name or the role of the agent, use the three attributes with the sub-elements label or role directly.
